spec.description: Daily units sold, 3 regions x 2 categories, 2023-2025. Multiplicative weekly + yearly seasonality, an upward trend, drifting Hijri-like holiday bumps and sporadic promo shocks, Poisson-sampled.

stationarity.name: Riyadh/Grocery (level)
stationarity.interpretation: ADF p=0.0023 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=0.

stationarity.name: Riyadh/Grocery (d=1)
stationarity.interpretation: ADF p=0.0000 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=1.

stationarity.name: Riyadh/Grocery (seasonal diff, D=1)
stationarity.interpretation: After one seasonal difference at lag 7: ADF p=0.0000 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=0.

decomposition.interpretation: STL at period 7: trend strength 0.668, seasonal strength 0.467 (Hyndman F_T/F_S, both in [0,1]; >0.6 is a strong component).

additive_vs_multiplicative.interpretation: |residual| still correlates with the trend at r=0.604 under an additive decomposition versus r=0.360 under a multiplicative one, so the multiplicative form leaves less level-dependence behind. That is the empirical case for a variance-stabilising transform before fitting an additive model.

acf_pacf.interpretation: 34 of the first 60 ACF lags and 29 PACF lags exceed the 95% band. Both functions tail off rather than cutting off cleanly (ACF significant through lag 16, PACF through lag 10), which points at a mixed ARMA rather than a pure AR or MA -- so the order is worth selecting by AIC over a small grid rather than read off the plot. Significant ACF spikes at lag(s) [7, 14, 21, 28] -- multiples of the seasonal period 7 -- confirm seasonal structure that a non-seasonal ARIMA cannot absorb, so a seasonal term is required.

spec.description: Monthly non-oil activity index, 2017-2025, 108 points. Linear trend, a 42-month business cycle plus an 11-month harmonic, and a 2020-shaped shock with partial exponential recovery.

skip_models.lgbm_global: Only one series -- a global model across series has nothing to pool. The per-series LightGBM is the honest comparison here.

stationarity.name: economic (level)
stationarity.interpretation: ADF p=0.7895 cannot reject a unit root and KPSS p<=0.010 rejects stationarity. Both point the same way: this series needs differencing, so d >= 1.

stationarity.name: economic (d=1)
stationarity.interpretation: ADF p=0.0000 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=1.

stationarity.name: economic (seasonal diff, D=1)
stationarity.interpretation: After one seasonal difference at lag 12: ADF p=0.0883 cannot reject a unit root, but neither does KPSS p>=0.100 reject stationarity -- the sample is not informative enough to separate the two. Treat d as a modelling choice to be settled by AIC rather than by these tests.

decomposition.interpretation: STL at period 12: trend strength 0.953, seasonal strength 0.078 (Hyndman F_T/F_S, both in [0,1]; >0.6 is a strong component).

additive_vs_multiplicative.interpretation: |residual| still correlates with the trend at r=0.078 under an additive decomposition versus r=0.217 under a multiplicative one, so the additive form leaves less level-dependence behind. That is the empirical case for fitting on the raw scale without a transform.

acf_pacf.interpretation: 9 of the first 36 ACF lags and 2 PACF lags exceed the 95% band. Both functions tail off rather than cutting off cleanly (ACF significant through lag 9, PACF through lag 1), which points at a mixed ARMA rather than a pure AR or MA -- so the order is worth selecting by AIC over a small grid rather than read off the plot.

spec.description: Daily spare-parts demand, 4 low-turnover SKUs, 2024-2025. 91.7%-97.9% zero rows depending on SKU; non-zero magnitudes are near-identical across SKUs, so essentially all the signal is *whether* an order occurs, not how large it is.

stationarity.name: SKU-C3087 (level)
stationarity.interpretation: ADF p=0.0000 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=0.

stationarity.name: SKU-C3087 (d=1)
stationarity.interpretation: ADF p=0.0000 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=1.

stationarity.name: SKU-C3087 (seasonal diff, D=1)
stationarity.interpretation: After one seasonal difference at lag 7: ADF p=0.0000 < 0.05 rejects the unit-root null, and KPSS p>=0.100 fails to reject stationarity. The two tests agree: no further differencing is needed at d=0.

decomposition.interpretation: STL at period 7: trend strength 0.002, seasonal strength 0.161 (Hyndman F_T/F_S, both in [0,1]; >0.6 is a strong component).

additive_vs_multiplicative.interpretation: A multiplicative decomposition is undefined here (the series contains zeros or negatives), so the additive form is the only option and no variance-stabilising transform is applied.

acf_pacf.interpretation: 4 of the first 60 ACF lags and 3 PACF lags exceed the 95% band. Significant ACF spikes at lag(s) [14] -- multiples of the seasonal period 7 -- confirm seasonal structure that a non-seasonal ARIMA cannot absorb, so a seasonal term is required.

mape_failure_demo.interpretation: Across 176 scored folds on a series that is 95.2% zeros, the median fold MAPE is 2,462,721,760% and the worst is 12,142,857,150% -- numbers with no usable interpretation, produced by dividing by actuals that are exactly zero. sMAPE is bounded at 162.4% median, which fails more politely without being more informative. WAPE's median of 125.2% is the only one of the three a planner could act on, because it divides total error by total volume once instead of row by row. 40 fold(s) had an all-zero test window, where even WAPE is only vacuously defined.
